quantization_notes.bits_per_parameter_theory_derivation: log2(3) — Shannon entropy of one ternary weight {-1,0,+1}; the theoretical lower bound, NOT the in-memory layout.
quantization_notes.memory_reduction_vs_fp16_derivation: 16 / 2 = 8.0x for a packed 2-bit-per-weight layout, plus small packing overhead; the 8.1x is the measured reduction, the honest headline for memory.
quantization_notes.reduction_if_theory_only_derivation: 16 / 1.58 = 10.13x — what the 1.58 entropy line implies if a reader trusts the theory denominator; NOT the shipped layout.

protocol.model: Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B (BitNet b1.58 continued-train, masked CE, deployed-forward QAT)
protocol.note: The three rows below are slices of the SAME training file (konstellation corpus, the file used for the continued-train), grouped by topic. There is ONE held-out val split (90 samples, stratified, same file); the row labels WikiText-2 / C4 / LAMBADA are convenience tags for the topic buckets, NOT three external corpora. If read as three external corpora the numbers would be invalid; read as topic slices of one file they are internally consistent.
protocol.val_split: 90-sample stratified held-out, same file as train

metal_gpu_throughput.note_bandwidth: Device peak sustained bandwidth (M3 Max memory system). This is a hardware ceiling, NOT a decode measurement.

measurement.effective_bandwidth_derivation: 0.1234 GB weights/token x 142.8 tok/s (0.5e9 params x 1.975 bits / 8 / 1e9)
measurement.bottleneck: NOT memory-bound at this size. 4.6% of peak means per-token overhead dominates — the normal situation for a half-billion-parameter decode. Memory-bound decoding would require a model ~20x larger.

70B_ceiling.note: This is a CEILING for what 70B would do IF it became memory-bound at peak bandwidth. The 0.5B run in this file (142.8 tok/s, 4.6% of peak) is nowhere near it. The 21.8x gap (3113 tok/s theoretical vs 142.8 actual) is the headroom a larger model could spend; the 70B row is a hardware bound, not a scale-check of the 0.5B run.
